name: Rite of Vision
summary: The Rite of Vision is a foundational spiritual trial undergone by young tauren stepping beyond the Red Cloud Mesa into greater Mulgore. To pierce the veil and receive guidance from ancestral spirits, initiates must gather natural reagents to brew the Water of the Seers under the watchful eye of Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village.

sections.title: The Reagents of the Land
sections.body: Before any vision can be granted, the initiate must demonstrate an intimate understanding of the natural gifts found across Mulgore. Zarlman Two-Moons instructs the seeker to collect well stones found near the sacred communal water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath the roots of Mulgore's ancient trees. These natural elements are not merely physical objects; to the tauren, they hold the latent magic and lifeblood of the Earth Mother, ready to be channeled into ritual use.

sections.title: Brewing the Water of the Seers
sections.body: Once gathered, Zarlman combines the stones and ambercorn into the potent Water of the Seers. When consumed beside the village's tribal flame, this ceremonial draft clears the mind and summons an ethereal guide. Following this manifestation across the plains forms the true heart of the rite, testing the initiate's ability to walk between the physical world and the spiritual whispers of the land.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Rite of Vision?
faq.answer: The Rite of Vision is a spiritual test for tauren coming of age and seeking their path. By preparing and drinking the Water of the Seers, the initiate learns to commune with spirits and follow ancestral omens across the plains of Mulgore.

Zarlman Two-Moons is a tauren shaman and seer stationed in Bloodhoof Village. He oversees spiritual trials for young adventurers, preparing ritual draughts such as the Water of the Seers and interpreting the signs of the Earth Mother.

faq.q: Where are well stones and ambercorn found?
faq.answer: Well stones are gathered from the ground near the freshwater wells scattered across Mulgore. Ambercorn can be found scattered at the bases of the large, sprawling trees dotting the surrounding grassy landscape.

faq.q: What happens after drinking the Water of the Seers?
aliases: what happens next rite of vision
faq.answer: Drinking the draft near the tribal fire opens the imbiber's spiritual sight, revealing a ghostly animal guide. The seeker must follow this spirit across the plains to uncover the next stage of their sacred journey.

faq.q: Why do the tauren revere water wells so deeply?
faq.answer: Water is the lifeblood of Mulgore and a precious gift of the Earth Mother. The wells serve as sacred communal centers that nourish both the land and its herds, making the stones gathered beside them spiritually charged.

faq.q: Does this quest lead to further rites?
aliases: next quest in rite of vision
is rite of vision a chain
faq.answer: Yes. This task is part of a multi-stage ceremony. Once Zarlman prepares the Water of the Seers, initiates must drink it, track the vision that appears, and present themselves to elder leaders across Mulgore.

angles.text: For tauren, the Rite of Vision is an essential cultural milestone, binding an emerging warrior, hunter, or mystic to the spiritual heritage of the Earth Mother and the ancestors.
Shaman will recognize the preparation of the Water of the Seers as a traditional grounding ritual, attuning the spirit to read unseen elements before conversing with spirits directly.
Druids hold deep reverence for the ambercorn and well stones, seeing them as direct manifestations of the flora and life-giving waterways that sustain Mulgore's balance.
